To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain galactocerebrosidosis (GC) in a patient with DDS was associated with the PASAD.

the galactolipoid ratio is increased in severe demyelination, and that this anomaly is not necessarily associated with sulfatide accumulation, but is probably related to the severity of the demyelination.

in DDS, as in other severe demyelina‐ting diseases, a galactolipide ratio is increased, which may be the cause of the disease, and that in PASAD the residual CS activity prevents the accumulation of sulfatide in the organ extracts, but not in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of the brain galac‐tolipid content in a patient with PASAD and DDS and in patients with MLD, adreno‐, and other leukodystrophies.
a new aspect of the biochemical pathology of the brain galac‐tolipids in DDS and MLD.

the study of the relationship between the residual activity of ASA and CS in organ tissues and in fibroblast homogenates and the content of brain galactolips in patients with DDS and other demyelinating brain diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ratio sulfatide/ga‐lactocerebrose in the brain is increased in severe de‐myleinating disorders of different etiology, and this is probably due to a disturbance in the biosynthesis and/or metabolism of galactolip­ids.
in the brain of the patient with PASAD and coincidental DDS the sulfatide/gala‐ctocerebroside ratio was elevated due to the increased sulfatide content.
the ratio of galactolipides in the brain tissue is a more specific marker of demyelinating disorders than the ratio of sulfatides/galactocer‐ebrosides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in severe demyelination the ratio of sulfatides/galactocer‐ebrerosides in the brain is elevated, but that this increase is not a consequence of sulfatide accumulation.

the galactolipide content in DDS, MLD, adrenoleukody‐trophy, and in the brain of the patient with PASAD, is not a simple function of the demyelination process but also depends on the residual ASA and CS activity.

the galactolipide sulfatide content is a sensitive marker for the severity of demyelinating processes in the brain, and that the galactocerebro‐side/sulfatide ratio in the brain is a more reliable marker for the severity and the course of these diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found that a patient who has a pseudo-arylsulfatse A deficiency (a disorder that causes sulfatides to accumulate in the brain) also has diffuse disseminated sclerosis.
the ratio of sulfatides to galactocerebro­side is a useful indicator of the severity of demyelination.
the brain galacto‐lipid content is a sensitive marker for demyelinating disorders, which is of importance in the diagnosis of these diseases and their follow‐up.
